headline: High-risk filesystem and network-enabled coding agent paired with a non-writing support agent creates prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure in shared project workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a writes and reads the project directory by default, and its self_isolation is none; agent_b has no file surfaces, so direct injection is not symmetric. However, the shared project directory creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in agent_a outputs can be consumed by agent_b if orchestrated externally. The pathway exists, but the pair lacks a documented direct channel, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are run against the same project directory, prompt-like content in files can cross from agent_a to agent_b.
IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate project directories per agent.
Strip instructions from generated files before handoff.
Use a human review step before agent_b consumes agent_a output.
Disable automatic file-to-prompt ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has broad network egress and can read/write the project directory, while agent_b has no filesystem or network surfaces. The main leakage path is agent_a exposing generated source code or secrets from the shared workspace to its configured model backend or external services; agent_b does not independently exfiltrate. Because the shared workspace exists and sensitive code may be present, the risk is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF sensitive source code is placed in the shared project directory, agent_a can transmit it to a third-party model backend.
IF agent_a is configured with external APIs, workspace contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory.
Use a local-only model for agent_a.
Rotate any credentials present in the workspace.
Restrict outbound network access for the session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-loss-prevention scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but agent_b cannot write, execute, or modify shared state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only overlap is readless/non-mutating interaction through an external orchestrator. Since the rubric’s high/medium conflict indicators require overlapping mutable resources, this pair is low risk for capability conflict.
conditions: IF agent_b is given write access outside its current profile, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable OAuth or filesystem target, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Avoid sharing writable directories.
Serialize any file edits through one agent.
Use lock files for any external orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces code and offers to run it, while agent_b is a support-oriented agent with no verification or tool authority in the profile. If agent_b is used to summarize or act on agent_a output, errors can cascade from generated code into downstream decisions. The pair does not show automatic action-taking, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b is prompted to treat agent_a output as authoritative, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF agent_a-generated code is copied into a workflow without review, incorrect assumptions can cascade.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before reuse of agent_a output.
Have a human review code before execution.
Ask agent_b to cite uncertainty in summaries.
Limit agent_a output to diffs, not full narratives.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles generated source code and may use OpenAI or another configured model, while agent_b has no declared data classes, no network egress, and no secrets. There is no documented residency or retention mismatch between them, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary vendor-processing concerns on agent_a alone. The pair does not show a clear cross-agent compliance breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_a prompts, vendor-processing obligations apply.
IF agent_b is later connected to a regulated datastore, compliance review must be repeated.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts.
Document the model vendor used by agent_a.
Keep agent_b disconnected from regulated datasets.
Review retention settings for agent_a.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls.
